package_info.package_name: MageCart JavaScript Skimmer (Euro Cup and Olympics Ticket Reseller)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (injected code, not a versioned package)
package_info.why_malicious: The injected JavaScript code is designed to steal payment card details from users of the ticket reseller website by intercepting form submissions and exfiltrating sensitive financial information to attacker-controlled infrastructure. This is a classic MageCart web skimmer attack targeting payment data at the point of entry.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when the user submits the payment form
execution_context.file_location: Injected JavaScript in the payment page (e.g., checkout.js or inline <script> tag on the payment/checkout page)
required_permissions: Access to the DOM to read form input fields
Ability to initiate outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the user submits the payment form, the code hooks the form submission event, reads credit card details directly from the DOM input fields, and sends the collected data via HTTPS POST to a hardcoded malicious domain, resulting in exfiltration of sensitive payment information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code intercepts the payment form submission, collects sensitive credit card data, and transmits it to an external, attacker-controlled domain. This behavior is characteristic of web skimming attacks and is not consistent with legitimate payment processing.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate e-commerce scripts should only transmit payment data to trusted payment processors or gateways, never to unknown or untrusted external domains. Directly accessing and exfiltrating raw credit card data from the DOM is a clear violation of security best practices.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate scripts may hook form submissions for client-side validation or to integrate with authorized payment gateways, but they do not send raw payment data to domains outside of the business or its payment partners.
key_indicators: Hooks the payment form's submit event handler
Directly accesses credit card input fields in the DOM
Sends sensitive data via fetch/XHR to a hardcoded, untrusted external domain
No user notification or consent for data transmission
Outbound HTTPS POST request from payment page to non-payment processor domain

attack_chain.action: Attacker injects malicious JavaScript into the ticket reseller's payment page, either by compromising the website or a third-party script.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of skimmer code in users' browsers when they visit the checkout page

attack_chain.action: The malicious JavaScript hooks the payment form's submit event to intercept user actions.
attack_chain.leads_to: Collection of payment card data from user input fields at the moment of form submission

attack_chain.action: The collected payment card data is sent via HTTPS POST to an attacker-controlled server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of sensitive financial information to the attacker's infrastructure

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code hooking form submission events specifically on payment or checkout pages
Outbound network requests (fetch/XHR) from payment pages to domains not associated with the business or its payment processors
Direct access to credit card input fields (e.g., input[name="cc_number"], input[name="cc_expiry"], input[name="cc_cvv"]) in the DOM by JavaScript
file_indicators: Unexpected or recently modified JavaScript files present on payment or checkout pages
Inline <script> tags containing obfuscated, minified, or unfamiliar code on sensitive pages
References to external JavaScript resources loaded from non-standard or untrusted domains
network_indicators: HTTPS POST requests from client browsers on checkout pages to domains not associated with the business or authorized payment processors (e.g., https://malicious-domain.com/collect)
Unusual or anomalous traffic patterns from payment pages to unknown endpoints, especially during form submission events
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Continuously monitor payment and checkout pages for unauthorized JavaScript modifications, including new or altered scripts that access credit card fields or initiate outbound requests to external domains. Implement and enforce a strict Content Security Policy (CSP) to restrict allowed destinations for outbound requests from sensitive pages. Analyze network traffic for POST requests to unfamiliar domains originating from payment or checkout pages. Regularly audit web assets and third-party scripts for unauthorized changes or injected code. Set up alerts for any script accessing payment input fields or sending data to non-whitelisted domains.
